'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine (2022–present)|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[missile strike]] on [[Sloviansk]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], kills at least two [[civilian]]s and injures 29 others. [https://www.euronews.com/2023/03/27/two-killed-and-29-wounded-in-shelling-of-eastern-ukrainian-city (Euronews)]
**The head of the [[Blagodarnensky District]] in [[Stavropol Krai]], [[Russia]], announces the death of Dmitry Lisitsky, commander of a battalion of the [[247th Guards Air Assault Regiment]] who participated in the 2014 [[Battle of Ilovaisk]]. [[Ukraine]] says that he was killed in battle while pro-Russian sources say that he committed [[suicide]]. [https://novayagazeta.eu/articles/2023/03/27/umer-rossiiskii-komandir-dmitrii-lisitskii-ego-nazyvaiut-odnim-iz-organizatorov-ilovaiskogo-kotla-na-vostoke-ukrainy-v-2014-godu-news (''Novaya Gazeta Europe'')]
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Six people are killed and several others are injured when a [[Suicide attack|suicide bomber]] [[detonate]]s himself near the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Afghanistan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] [[headquarters]] in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/3/27/blast-near-afghanistan-foreign-ministry-kills-at-least-two-ngo (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least seven people are killed by a [[landslide]] in [[Alausí]], [[Chimborazo Province]], [[Ecuador]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-65088388 (BBC News)]
*A train transporting hazardous materials derails near [[Wyndmere, North Dakota]], [[United States]], with 31 out of 70 train cars damaged. [https://www.kare11.com/article/news/local/train-derailment-hazardous-materials-in-north-dakota/89-35ea8e28-b5c9-46fd-b190-4779c85fe225 (KARE-TV)]
*Eleven people are killed after a fire breaks out in a warehouse in [[Cang County]], [[Hebei]], [[China]]. [https://apnews.com/article/hebei-warehouse-fire-11-died-2228dceb7237766b175700c7364acc75 (AP)]
*Twenty people are killed and around 29 others are injured after a bus crashes and overturns in [['Asir Province]], [[Saudi Arabia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/3/28/bus-carrying-pilgrims-crashes-in-saudi-kills-20 (Al Jazeera)]
'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Taiwan]]
**[[Cross-Strait relations]]
***Former [[President of the Republic of China|Taiwanese President]] [[Ma Ying-jeou]] becomes the first [[Taiwan]]ese leader to visit [[mainland China]] since the end of the [[Chinese Civil War]] in 1949, meeting with China's [[Taiwan Affairs Office]] deputy chair Chen Yuanfeng in [[Shanghai]]. Taiwan's ruling [[Democratic Progressive Party]] criticized this visit as "endorsing" China's position on Taiwan. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/3/27/former-taiwan-leader-arrives-in-china-first-such-trip-in-decades (Al Jazeera)]
**[[President of Honduras|Honduran President]] [[Xiomara Castro]] orders Taiwanese diplomats to vacate the country's embassy in [[Tegucigalpa]] within 30 days, [[Dates of establishment of diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China|one day after the country established diplomatic relations]] with the [[China|People's Republic of China]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/taiwan-told-vacate-embassy-honduras-after-ties-severed-2023-03-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[Enlargement of NATO]]
**[[Finland–Hungary relations]]
***The [[National Assembly (Hungary)|National Assembly]] of [[Hungary]] votes 182–6 to approve [[Finland]]'s accession to [[NATO]], leaving [[Turkey]] as the last remaining NATO member to approve Finland's membership in the [[military alliance]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20230327-hungarian-parliament-approves-finland-s-nato-membership-bid (France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Covenant School shooting]]
**Six people are killed in a [[mass shooting]] at the Covenant School in [[Nashville]], [[Tennessee]], [[United States]]. The suspect is later killed by responding police officers. [https://edition.cnn.com/us/live-news/nashville-shooting-covenant-school-03-27-23/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Burkina Faso]] suspends [[France 24]] broadcasts after the news agency aired an interview with the leader of [[al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb]] earlier this month. The [[Burkinabé government]] accused France 24 of being a "mouthpiece for [[terrorist]]s" and "[[hate speech]]", which the agency denies as "unfounded". [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/burkina-faso-suspends-france-24-broadcasts-country-after-al-qaeda-interview-2023-03-27/ (Reuters)]
*One person is killed and five others are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] at a school in [[São Paulo]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazilian-teen-stabs-teacher-death-wounds-five-others-school-2023-03-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Israeli anti-judicial reform protests]]
**[[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] announces a pause on [[government of Israel|his government]]'s [[2023 Israeli judicial reform|controversial judicial reform bill]] until April 30, the opening of the [[Knesset]]'s summer session. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2023/03/27/israel-netanyahu-strikes-protests-judicial-reform-defense-minister/11548472002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[2023 Scottish National Party leadership election]]
**[[Cabinet Secretary for NHS Recovery, Health and Social Care|Health and Social Care Secretary]] [[Humza Yousaf]] is elected as the new leader of the [[Separatism in the United Kingdom|separatist]] [[Scottish National Party]], defeating [[Cabinet Secretary for Finance and the Economy|Finance Secretary]] [[Kate Forbes]] with 52.1% of the vote. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-65086551 (BBC News)]
*The [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|Iraqi Parliament]] passes 206–12 a series of amendments reducing the electoral districts in each [[Governorates of Iraq|governorate]] to one, ahead of local elections in November. Voting blocs and independent members who boycotted the vote claim the amendments make it more difficult for the opposition to get elected.  [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/3/27/iraqi-parliament-passes-controversial-vote-law-amendments (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Censorship of TikTok]], [[Censorship of Twitter]]
**[[France]] [[Internet censorship in France|bans]] the use of [[Instagram]], [[TikTok]], [[Twitter]], and other apps on [[Government of France|government]] employees' phones due to concerns relating to insufficient [[data security]] measures. [https://apnews.com/article/tiktok-france-ban-cybersecurity-china-4c48564fbfe7b86bf44c30969902c293 (AP)]
*Scientists discover [[lunar water]] samples in tiny glass beads from the [[Moon]] in studies published by the ''[[Nature Geoscience]]'' journal. [https://abcnews.go.com/Technology/wireStory/new-source-water-found-moon-samples-china-mission-98162299 (ABC News)]
